meaning: Rss (sagittal-sinus outflow resistance) is pinned to 212.8 dyn·s/mL, the Brain_1 build-time default, instead of the cascade-consistent (Psinus − Pcv)/Q value. This keeps M7 on the same venous outflow resistance every fitted M1 run used, so the NN compliance is trained against the same baseline.

could_move.what: Rest ICP level: the comment records that the cascade value instead moved patient 137's rest ICP from 7.9 to 12.5 mmHg
M1-vs-M7 comparison decks: if the two models used different Rss, differences credited to the NN compliance would be confounded
The M1 reference this is anchored to, where the same default is taken implicitly rather than written out
Jugular-compression response, since Rss sits in the same outflow path as the IJV tube parameters set just below

expectation: Against the cascade value, this choice lowers rest ICP by about 4.6 mmHg in the one documented case (137: 12.5 → 7.9). Whether that sign and size carry to other patients, or to pulse amplitudes, is unknown from this context.

check.why: Replots the one deck where M7 is compared to M1 for patient 137, the case the comment quotes rest-ICP numbers for. Cheaper than a re-fit and shows whether rest ICP and the M1/M7 offset still look like the fitted baseline.
